result.topic_en: Euler concludes his discussion of the free-ended rod's tones and begins Case V: a vibrating elastic rod with one end simply fixed (pinned) and the other firmly clamped, setting up the boundary-condition equations.

vix vnquam audietur, ita vt tantum duplex octaua ſimul
cum fundamentali tinniat. Talis igitur virga ſonos mul-
to puriores reddere eſt cenſenda quam chordae ſimplices,
vnde etiam ſoni hoc modo editi in muſica peculiarem
ſuauitatem habere debebunt.

Euolutio caſus V.
quo virgae elaſticae alter terminus ſimpliciter eſt
fixus, alter vero quaſi muro firmiter infixus.

Problema.
§. 39. Si virgae elaſticae terminus E fuerit ſim-
pliciter fixus, alter vero F prorſus infixus, inueſtigare omnes
motus, quibus ea contremiſcere poteſt.

Solutio.
Quia terminus E, vbi fit $s=0$, ſimpliciter eſt fixus,
habebimus ſtatim, vti in caſu praecedente, $\beta=-\alpha$ et $\delta=0$;
pro altero autem termino, vbi $s=a$, erit tam $y=0$ quam
$\left(\frac{dy}{ds}\right)=0$, vnde poſito $\frac{a}{f}=\omega$ oriuntur hae duae aequa-
tiones:
$\alpha e^{\omega}+\beta e^{-\omega}+\gamma \sin.\omega+\delta \cos.\omega=0,$
$\alpha e^{\omega}-\beta e^{-\omega}+\gamma \cos.\omega-\delta \sin.\omega=0,$
quae, ſubſtitutis praecedentibus valoribus, abeunt in has:
$\alpha(e^{\omega}-e^{-\omega})+\gamma \sin.\omega=0$ et
$\alpha(e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega})+\gamma \cos.\omega=0.$
Ex

items.quote:
Si virgae elaſticae terminus E fuerit ſim-
pliciter fixus, alter vero F prorſus infixus, inueſtigare omnes
motus, quibus ea contremiſcere poteſt.
items.english: If the end E of an elastic rod is simply fixed, while the other end F is completely clamped, to investigate all the motions with which it can vibrate.

items.quote:
Talis igitur virga ſonos mul-
to puriores reddere eſt cenſenda quam chordae ſimplices,
vnde etiam ſoni hoc modo editi in muſica peculiarem
ſuauitatem habere debebunt.
items.english: Such a rod must therefore be judged to give much purer sounds than simple strings, whence also sounds produced in this way ought to have a peculiar sweetness in music.
